newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil mostly firmer, German DIN leads the way.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil mostly firmer, German DIN leads the way.

text.p: German heating oil cargo premiums held on to recent gains on Friday, but the stronger sentiment failed to knock on to the barge market where differentials made only modest gains.
Heating oil barges traded at April IPE -75 cents and -50 cents a tonne fob ARA, slightly up on Thursday's traded levels.

A German heating oil cargo traded late on Thursday at April IPE +$6.50 a tonne, a leap of around $4 on recent levels. The buyer of the 10,000 tonne DIN cargo said that he also bought 20,000 tonnes of similar material earlier in the week at April +$6.
Traders said that the movement of some 250,000 tonnes of Russian gas oil from the Baltic to Asia this month helped to keep the heat under differentials.
"There's just a little bit of (heating oil) material from Scandinavia and the U.K. suitable for Germany," a dealer said.
German DIN was actively talked around the firmer levels, with first half April discussed at April IPE +$5/$7 a tonne but no deals were concluded.

But discussion on FOD premiums were thin with French buyers sticking to the sidelines. Differentials were assessed around April IPE +$2/$3, while EN590 was pegged at April +$11.50/$12.50 a tonne cif Le Havre.
German diesel barges were talked slightly firmer at April IPE +$12.50/$13.00, while Benelux spec barges were discussed at a $1 discount.
IPE gas oil futures barely shifted on Friday, with April last traded 25 cents up at $169.50 a tonne.
